title: ClawHavoc: 341 malicious skills on OpenClaw's ClawHub marketplace deliver infostealers through fake prerequisites
summary: Koi Security audited 2,857 skills on OpenClaw's ClawHub marketplace and found 341 malicious ones in a campaign named ClawHavoc; 335 used fake prerequisites that told macOS users to paste a script installing Atomic Stealer and Windows users to download a password-protected archive containing a keylogging trojan, while other skills hid reverse shells inside working code or exfiltrated the agent's ~/.clawdbot/.env credentials to a webhook. ClawHub is open by default and only requires a publisher's GitHub account to be at least one week old; OpenClaw's response was a reporting feature that auto-hides skills with more than three unique reports.
verification_note: URL fetched 2026-10-17; headline, byline (Ravie Lakshmanan), date Feb 02 2026, and the 2,857 / 341 / 335 figures confirmed from the article body. The candidate's claims that OpenClaw later added VirusTotal scanning and that the 335 skills delivered a Windows keylogger are not on the page and were dropped; the page attributes the keylogging trojan to the Windows download path and Atomic Stealer to the macOS path.
